skill.name: mtls-configuration
skill.description: Configure mutual TLS (mTLS) for zero-trust service-to-service communication. Use when implementing zero-trust networking, certificate management, or securing internal service communication.
skill.summary: Configure and troubleshoot mutual TLS for service meshes and zero-trust service communication.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Most static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown fences, example paths, placeholders, and reference links. The review confirms an all-interface bind and identifies unsafe mTLS bypass examples and insufficient CA key protection guidance.

remediation.issue: The SPIRE example binds its server to every network interface.
remediation.suggestion: Use a scoped interface and require network policy or firewall restrictions around the SPIRE server port.

remediation.issue: Examples permit plaintext traffic or bypass mesh TLS without compensating controls.
remediation.suggestion: Label every exception as temporary and require authorization, network policy, monitoring, and a removal deadline.

remediation.issue: The CA signing key example uses a standard Kubernetes Secret without protection guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend an external key manager or encrypted secrets with strict RBAC, audit logging, backup protection, and rotation procedures.

semantic_findings.title: mTLS Bypass Examples Lack Compensating Controls
semantic_findings.description: Examples permit plaintext mesh traffic and bypass Linkerd TLS without requiring authorization, network isolation, monitoring, or a removal deadline.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples explicitly use PERMISSIVE, DISABLE, and skip-outbound-ports settings. These settings can allow traffic outside mutual authentication.

semantic_findings.title: CA Signing Key Protection Is Underspecified
semantic_findings.description: The template places CA signing material in a standard Kubernetes Secret without guidance for encryption, strict access control, auditing, or external key storage.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The example creates a CA issuer backed by a Secret containing tls.key. Compromise of that key can undermine the mesh trust domain.

content.user_title: Configure Mutual TLS for Service Meshes
content.value_statement: Service-to-service encryption is difficult to configure consistently across mesh platforms. This skill provides mTLS templates, certificate guidance, verification commands, and troubleshooting steps.
actual_capabilities: Explains the mutual TLS handshake and certificate hierarchy.
Provides Istio PeerAuthentication and DestinationRule templates.
Shows cert-manager certificate issuance patterns for Istio workloads.
Provides an abbreviated SPIFFE and SPIRE deployment example.
Includes Linkerd configuration and certificate inspection commands.
Lists commands for diagnosing mesh authentication and TLS failures.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to cluster names, namespaces, identities, and trust domains.
The referenced implementation playbook is not included in the reported file structure.
The skill does not deploy resources or verify a live cluster.
Production certificate storage and access controls require environment-specific security review.

use_cases.title: Enforce Istio mTLS
use_cases.description: Create strict mesh and workload authentication policies with controlled migration settings.

use_cases.title: Operate Workload Certificates
use_cases.description: Plan certificate issuance, renewal, rotation, and trust hierarchy for Kubernetes services.

use_cases.title: Diagnose TLS Failures
use_cases.description: Inspect mesh policies, proxy certificates, identities, logs, and service connections.

prompt_templates.title: Explain mTLS
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain mutual TLS for two Kubernetes services. Describe identity verification, certificate trust, and encrypted communication.
prompt_templates.scenario: Learn the core flow before selecting a service mesh.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Istio Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Istio strict mTLS policy for namespace [namespace] and workload [workload]. Include verification steps and rollback guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Certificate Rotation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design certificate rotation for [platform] with [certificate lifetime]. Include renewal timing, monitoring, failure handling, and CA rotation.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Multi-Cluster Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this multi-cluster mTLS design: [design]. Identify trust boundaries, bypasses, key risks, observability gaps, and validation tests.

output_examples.input: Enable strict Istio mTLS for the payments namespace.
output: A namespace policy that requires mutual TLS.
A staged migration plan from permissive mode.
Verification commands for authentication policy and proxy state.

output_examples.input: Investigate failed calls between two Linkerd workloads.
output: Identity and edge checks for both workloads.
Proxy log checks for certificate and handshake errors.
A concise list of likely causes and corrective actions.

output_examples.input: Plan short-lived certificates for an Istio workload.
output_examples.output: A certificate lifecycle plan covering issuance, renewal, expiry alerts, CA trust, rotation testing, and recovery procedures.

best_practices: Start migration in permissive mode, measure plaintext traffic, then enforce strict mode with a deadline.
Use short-lived workload certificates and monitor renewal failures before expiration.
Protect CA keys with strong access controls, encryption, auditing, and regular rotation.
anti_patterns: Do not disable mutual TLS on production ports without documented compensating controls.
Do not store real private keys in prompts, repositories, logs, or unencrypted configuration.
Do not apply generic templates before validating identities, ports, namespaces, and trust boundaries.

faq.question: What is mutual TLS?
faq.answer: Mutual TLS encrypts a connection and requires both peers to present trusted certificates.

faq.question: Which service meshes are covered?
faq.answer: The skill provides examples for Istio and Linkerd, plus SPIFFE and SPIRE integration guidance.

faq.question: Does the skill generate certificates?
faq.answer: No. It provides configuration patterns and operational guidance for certificate issuance and rotation.

faq.question: Can I use the templates unchanged?
faq.answer: No. Replace example namespaces, identities, paths, domains, ports, and policy exceptions before deployment.

faq.question: How should private keys be handled?
faq.answer: Use protected key storage, strict access control, encryption, auditing, and rotation. Never place real keys in prompts.

faq.question: How do I verify mTLS?
faq.answer: Inspect mesh authentication policies, proxy identities, certificate validity, connection edges, and TLS-related logs.
